generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: an introduced biennial: a rosette of soft, hairy leaves, then a tall spire of hanging, purple-pink tubular flowers. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1.4 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: grey-green leaves; purple-pink flowers spotted inside.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

generator.program.note: The program the spec's authors chose to grow this form.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: The Flora of New Zealand (vol. IV, Webb and others 1988), as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): corolla campanulate, inflated above a constricted base, 3.5 to 5 cm long, its lobes short and rounded; 4 stamens; a calyx of 5. King's American Dispensatory (1898) adds the limb oblique and 2-lipped, the upper lip notched, the lower 3-lobed with its middle lobe the largest, and a 2-celled ovary with one style; the Plantaginaceae's superior ovary.

appearance.organs.flower.shape.note: Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5): a two-lipped bell from the characters by the rules at the flowering plants. By hand: the tube joined for most of the petals' length and a little swollen, since the Flora of New Zealand gives the lobes short and the tube inflated above its base; the sepals much shorter than the corolla, as King's American Dispensatory has them (as search results quote them; the pages themselves were not read).
